correctness.rationale: For all positive n,k, telescoping yields H_{n,k,2k}=[n+1]_{q^k} Q_{n,k}^2/[2k]_q with Q=product_{m=1}^n[k]_{q^m}. At n=1 this equals [k]_q. At n>=2 the ratio is [n+1]_{q^k}[k]_q^2[k]_{q^2}R^2/(1+q). If n odd, factor [n+1]_{q^k}=(1+q^k)[(n+1)/2]_{q^{2k}} to obtain a product of q-integers; if k even, factor [k]_q=(1+q)[k/2]_{q^2} to obtain a product of q-integers. Both have nonnegative integer coefficients. For even n and odd k, the numerator at q=-1 equals k^(n-1), proving a genuine simple pole and necessity. Comparison with gcd(n,2k)|k gives exactly the claimed false-negative locus. The bundled VERIFY.py independently checked 48 exact polynomial identities and 1,800 cyclotomic-exponent criteria; finite checks are not the infinite proof.
